product_description: The Acer Iconia Tab A13 is a large screen Android tablet designed for entertainment, learning, and productivity, running Android 15 on a five core Allwinner A333 processor clocked up to 1.8GHz with integrated graphics for fluid navigation across apps, streaming video, and casual gaming. Encased in a narrow bezel Shale Black aluminum alloy chassis just 8mm thin and weighing 1.34 pounds, the tablet pairs a sleek, book friendly profile with the durability needed for daily use at home or in the classroom. Its centerpiece is the 13 inch IPS touch display, which renders WUXGA 1920 by 1200 resolution at 350 nits of brightness across a 16 by 10 aspect ratio, giving movies, documents, and games plenty of vivid, detailed screen real estate. Powering that experience is 4GB of LPDDR4X onboard memory alongside 64GB of eMMC storage, with a microSD card slot available to expand capacity by up to 512GB for downloaded media, apps, and files. Dual band 802.11ax Wi-Fi 6 with MU-MIMO technology and Bluetooth 5.4 provide dependable wireless connectivity, while a 2 megapixel front camera and 5 megapixel rear camera handle video calls and casual photography with ease. A 5,000mAh lithium ion battery delivers up to 10 hours of video playback on a single charge, and Widevine L1 certification enables full high definition streaming from platforms such as Netflix and Disney Plus. Google Kids Space adds a parent managed space for younger users, rounding out a tablet built to serve students and families across a wide range of everyday tasks.

reviews.title: Not durable
reviews.content: Child had this at college for a month and the screen is already busted. It was not dropped. A corner of the screen got knocked slightly, which should not have been enough to cause so much damage. We have Dell laptops (also 2-in-1 type with touch screen) that have handled being knocked on the floor, water spilled on the keyboard, all kinds of things and don’t have a scratch. Meanwhile, this device broke at the slightest inkling of more than the lightest touch. Repair cost is absurd and HP customer service was very pushy about getting it done. Almost like it’s part of their business model.

reviews.title: Great computer, fast, chic

reviews.title: Hasn't worked since it was taken out of the box
reviews.content: It has been less than 2 months since it was delivered and this "paperweight" is at HP for repairs. There is nothing good that I can say about this laptop other than it was delivered quickly. Otherwise, nothing but issues and HP support is no better than the laptop. Wasn't able to unbox right away due to a health issue so I missed the 15 day window return or this thing would have been returned!!!!! Took hours to get it to boot up first time boxed it back up and was heading to Best Buy when I was told I only had 15 days, I was at day 18. So back to trying to get this thing to work. It will take several tries to get it to go to the home screen. Every startup there is an error something is wrong, diagnosis, sorry can't diagnose. If it does make it past "can't diagnose" it says "repairing" only to say "sorry, can't repair but don't worry we have undone all the changes" Great so you can't repair something so put it back to broke, perfect! It says updating Bios, then sorry unable to update Bios. EVERY TIME YOU START IT UP! After weeks of searching HP help boards, and help boards period to see what the errors it is giving me means, one says that the chips in these don't speak microsoft and translates it into whatever language it speaks which will cause "issues" , one of the other errors it gives me at start up says that it is a "critical hardware failure" and I need to replace motherboard/SSD etc. It will also drop the wi-fi and bluetooth whenever it feels like DAILY which requires the thing to be powered off over 3 times up to as many times as it takes to get the wi-fi and bluetooth to reappear. What do I mean by reappear? I mean not only does it drop the wi-fi and bluetooth the tabs to turn them back on COMPLETELY disappear and if you try to use the diagnostics, it shows my wi-fi and bluetooth devices but tells me that there is no wi-fi or bluetooth on the tablet and to contact HP support. After 2 plus hours on the phone, installing drivers, The tech has me video calling with her so she can "see" and she said yes, nothing you can do this needs to come in for repairs. Send it in with a detailed 2 page book report of what it is doing, what the errors are telling me only to have them a week later email that they can't get it to reproduce the issue, can I explain 1) what issues are you having 2) when does it happen 3) how can they replicate the issue. q_a.question: Can a 2nd SSD be added? Is there another m.2 slot available?
q_a.answer: No 2nd slot, but you can upgrade the in-place drive up to 4TB. Just be sure that you use a single-sided SSD. Double-sided chips are glued to both sides of the stick, making it physically too thick to screw flat onto your laptop's board, and forcing a double-sided drive down can flex the motherboard or press dangerously hard against your laptop's battery cell or under-chassis.

reviews.title: Really good deal with one catch (ssd)
reviews.content:
With $100 off at Best Buy, these were the best deal on a Windows laptop for $6-700 at the time I purchased. All of the laptops in this price range have some huge drawback to make them cheap, but these didn't have an obvious one. After taking it home and at first thinking it was Windows on ARM making it slow and weird, I inspected the SSD. It's actually eMMC memory (like an SD card) on an SSD chip. AKA really, really slow. I tested mine at 1400MB read and 600MB write. That's about like an SD card from 2018.

Besides that, there is no catch. I was comparing directly to a MacBook Neo that I have been testing since launch. The Snapdragon drivers have evolved considerably and I was able to load every program and game I tested. The base Snapdragon X is definitely meant for productivity laptops, but it no longer has any trouble starting games and heavy applications. The gaming and encoding performance is now about what you would expect for the power of the chip. I found it very, very similar to the a18 Pro in the MacBook Neo, making it a pretty good ARM to ARM comparison on Windows vs Mac, OS aside.

The screen is definitely the best feature of these laptops. The 1200p OLED screen is definitely the bottom end of OLED screens, but that still makes it dramatically better than the standard in sub-$1000 laptops. In my testing it was actually significantly brighter than listed, at about 350 nits.

Overall the OmniBook 3 series with Snapdragon X is really competitive, but I wouldn't buy unless you either have a spare ssd that is faster to put in, or are factoring a replacement into the cost. A drive that slow makes the operating system performance, sleep and wake times and even program loading lag noticeably.

reviews.title: A Laptop That Exceeded My Expectations!
reviews.content:
I absolutely love my HP OmniBook X Flip! I had been looking for a laptop that could handle school, work, multitasking, and everyday use while still feeling premium and enjoyable to use, and this laptop has exceeded my expectations.

The 16" 2K OLED touchscreen is easily one of my favorite features. The display is absolutely beautiful, with vibrant colors, excellent contrast, and plenty of screen space for having multiple windows open. Everything from working on documents and spreadsheets to watching movies looks fantastic. The touchscreen and 2-in-1 design are also incredibly convenient and make the laptop much more versatile.

Performance has been excellent so far. The Intel Core Ultra 5, 16GB of memory, and 512GB SSD make everyday tasks feel fast and responsive, even when I have multiple applications and browser tabs open at the same time. I also really appreciate having Copilot+ features built in.

The Eclipse Gray finish gives it a sleek, professional look, and the overall build quality makes it feel like a much more expensive laptop. I especially appreciate that it manages to combine a large, gorgeous display with the flexibility of a 2-in-1.

As a college student, this has been an especially great fit for me. It gives me the screen real estate I want for school and work without sacrificing the features and flexibility that make it enjoyable to use every day.

Overall, I am extremely happy with this purchase. The combination of the OLED display, performance, touchscreen, 2-in-1 design, and premium feel makes this one of the best laptops I've owned. I would absolutely recommend the HP OmniBook X Flip to anyone looking for a powerful, versatile, and genuinely enjoyable laptop!

reviews.title: Excellent Battery Life and Screen... but 60hz
reviews.content:
Real world battery life is fantastic. Without making any effort to conserve battery, I was getting roughly 2 hours for every 10% drop in battery life during light use (web browsing with Chrome, watching videos) with balanced power settings in Windows. Really liked the small, lightweight power brick that can still add a decent amount of charge in a short time. The keyboard is very good, in my opinion, and much improved over the totally flat version in the previous generation. Touchscreen works well, and it's pretty fun to use as a comically large tablet when kicking back on the couch. Speakers are good enough to get the job done, but my expectations for laptop speakers are pretty low though so take that for what you will. 

16 gigs of memory and a 512GB SSD feel inadequate for the price, but given how expensive memory and storage have become I suppose those amounts are actually reasonable. Regardless, both are enough for the sort of lightweight tasks the rest of the hardware is suited to anyway. The OLED display really wows with its contrast especially, but a 60hz refresh rate feels inadequate in 2026. I haven't purchased a display with less than 120hz in 10+ years at this point, so the lack of smoothness feels very noticeable to me even just scrolling websites etc.

I ended up returning this one, in spite of the fact that I really liked it overall. Why? Well, it went on sale for over $200 less than I paid for it, and Best Buy could not (would not?) price match the difference because I traded in my old laptop at the same time... but I could still return it. Was planning to just buy the same one again for $200 less, but then found the substantially upgraded model with double the ram, storage, and a 3k 120hz OLED on sale for a couple hundred more than I paid originally. So I went with that one instead.

reviews.title: Great laptop, bad Best Buy delivery
reviews.content: Great computer, no complaints with the computer but Best Buy service and delivery process is not the best. I purchased this laptop on a weekend. Notifications said the delivery was the following Wednesay via UPS Roadie courier. I skipped some appointments and came home early. The Roadie notifications showed the laptop was delivered just before I got home. In my driveway was a Best Buy sealed box that should have contained the laptop and a keyboard. When I opened the box, no computer, just the keyboard. When you try to contact Best Buy customer service, the store can't help and the online resource dosent tell you what to do about a missing item. They only provide options for support of the product once you have it. I spent hours asking the Best Buy chat for support but got nowhere. Luckily my wife works as customer support for another company and started asking for a manager. After that, we got in touch with a real person (still not a manager) via the chat tool who was understanding. I was ready to file a police report as the computer is more than $500 and the box was sealed when I got it but the agent insistend a report was unnessary and a replacement laptop would be sent. The next day, Thursday I received a notification about the replacmement delivering to me the next Sunday. I waited patiently until Sunday. Sunday morning I received a notification that the delivery was delayed. LSince I was not far from the store in Cumming Ga where the laptop was coming from I thought I would make things easier and pick it up myself. I got to the store and the people there could not help me. I was there for about 40 - 60 minutes. I was told there was a system error showing on the store end and there was nothing that could be done for me. I went back home l, went online, started the Best Buy chat tool and asked for another manager. The agent ( not a manager), said they thought there was an inventory or process error and reset the order for store pickup. About midday the following Monday the laptop was confirmed ready. I finally picked it up later that Monday. When I decided to buy from Best Buy, I did so because I didnt trust Amazon's delivery process. Best Buy let me down. I am happy things worked out in the end but this purchase took way more of my time than it should have. I will be very hesitant to purchase from Best Buy again.

q_a.question: Does this laptop have the capability to type words that are spoken to the computer?
q_a.answer:
EVERY Windows computer has that capability. 

Without going into details on how to use it:
1.It's called "Voice Typing." You activate it by using the shortcut "Windows Key + H", or searching the term in Programs/Apps. It will type what you say in Word, a browser, or email. You must be online at all times to use it.

2.If you are offline, you can also use Voice Access (Win11 only), which also allows you to control the computer (no mouse or keypad necessary), but you must be online the first time to download the local language model. More control, but a bit slower for actual dictation, and provides privacy if you are dictating sensitive information. Also, you have to be in a quiet room, since it will pick up transient noises in the area (a classroom, other people speaking in the room, podcasts or music you might like to listen to while working, etc.). And be sure to put it to sleep when not in use; otherwise, like an Echo, it will listen continuously.

reviews.title: Handy and portable
reviews.content:
I purchased the Neo for college because I can’t drag my ten pound PC everywhere to do work when I’m not home. So far, I enjoy my Neo and am pleased with it but I do still have my complaints and things I’m just not used to as I’ve only every used a laptop or pc that ran on windows so this is a change for me. My favorite things about the Neo so far is the color (I recommend getting a case as mine got scratched up fairly easy/early on from being in my backpack), the setup of the screen (widgets and controls especially because they are almost the same as my iPhone), how easy it is to pack and open up, and how I can access things that I normally would only be able to use on my iPhone (messages, emails, FaceTime, etc.). 
The list of complaints are longer than my compliments but they are small things because I don’t have a history with Macs. One thing I have noticed is that I can never close the Finder app which is annoying. Closing tabs is an interesting task too because I have to press the “close tab” button and then have to double click the pad over the tab I closed that’s in the dock and select “quit” for it to actually close the app. Another thing is if I wanted to put  (for example) the notes app for in the dock but not fully close it then I have to “exit full screen”, and then press the “minimize” button, but I don’t think there is any way to keep something full screen when you close it and open it back up again without having to press an extra button. I must say that being able to access my phone through my laptop is cool but half of the apps you have on your phone that you might want to use on your laptop can only be used if you turn your phone off, open it, and then connect It to the Neo and after all that I might as well as use my phone… There is no usb A cord slots (rectangular one) and there are only two usb c ones plus one for a headphone cord, which means that you have to buy and carry around a port hub. My last issue is how long it takes me to open the dock… I swear it takes forever for the dock to pop up and I end up having to swipe my finger on the pad downwards at least three times before the dang thing shows up. (I wish Apple added more accessories for the Neo included with your purchase in the box…I miss when Apple used to take care of us)

reviews.title: MacBook
reviews.content:
I have been absolutely loving my MacBook Air! I was looking for a laptop that would be reliable for school but also work well for all of my creative projects, and this has been a great choice. It is lightweight and easy to carry around, which is especially nice when I have to take it with me throughout the day. It starts up quickly, runs smoothly, and I can have multiple tabs and programs open without it feeling slow.
One of my favorite things about it is the display. Everything looks so clear and bright, which makes a huge difference when I’m working on Canva designs, looking at photos, or watching Netflix. I also really appreciate the battery life because I don’t have to constantly worry about finding an outlet while I’m working or doing schoolwork.
I use my MacBook Air for so many different things, including school assignments, Google Docs, research, Canva, creative projects, streaming, and just everyday browsing. It has been able to handle everything I’ve needed it for without any issues. I also love how well it works with my iPhone and other Apple devices. Being able to easily access photos, copy and paste between devices, and keep everything connected is really convenient.
Another thing I like is how clean and simple the MacBook Air feels. It doesn’t feel bulky or complicated, and it’s easy to customize it to what I need. The keyboard is comfortable to type on, the trackpad is really smooth, and the overall design feels high quality. It also looks great sitting on my desk!
The only downsides for me are that it can be expensive compared to some other laptops, and I wish it had more built-in ports. However, those are pretty minor compared to everything I like about it. Overall, I’m extremely happy with my MacBook Air and feel like it was a great investment for school, creativity, entertainment, and everyday use. I would definitely recommend it to anyone looking for a reliable laptop that can do a little bit of everything!

I recently purchased the Apple MacBook Pro 14-inch with the M5 Pro chip from the Best Buy store in Anchorage, Alaska, and the entire experience reminded me why sometimes a purchase really can live up to the name on the building.

It is powerful without being cumbersome, beautifully designed without sacrificing practicality, and after spending time with it, I am extremely pleased with my decision.

Just as importantly, my experience with Best Buy in Anchorage made an already exciting purchase even better. Buying a premium computer is an investment, and I appreciated having a purchasing experience that left me feeling confident about what I was bringing home rather than simply feeling as though I had completed another transaction.

There is something satisfying about making a significant purchase and, afterward, having absolutely no buyer’s remorse—only the feeling that you made the right choice.

In this case, I can say it quite literally:

My new MacBook Pro from Best Buy truly was a “Best Buy.”

Five stars for an excellent product and an excellent purchasing experience. I could not be happier with my new MacBook Pro.

The 60-day AppleCare+ enrollment window had also closed weeks before my purchase, so extended coverage was never available to me. This tablet is of course extremely powerful. the most powerful tablet you can buy even in late 2026. It does handle more like a laptop however due to the weight and thickness, but the touch screen is amazing, and there's a lot of flexibility. It's relatively quiet though the fans are noticeable at top speeds, which will definitely kick in while gaming, so keep that in mind if you plan to use this with anyone else in the room. 

Most modern games play best in 1080p, which still looks great on the small screen, but not so great if you plan to doc on a larger monitor. If that's the plan, go with a true gaming laptop. This thing is meant to be portable, with gaming happening right on its screen, so it's all about massive power in a small form factor.

This device truly delivered. Really wanted to consolidate all of my devices both for travel and simplicity. Was considering the Microsoft Surface heavily until a Best Buy associate listened to my use case and recommended the Z13 Flow. I wasn’t sure it was for me at first but after a little research I decided to pull the trigger and committed to giving it a fair shot.

Super glad I did. The device performs amazing well all around and for those that travel, the detachable keyboard with kickstand is a massive win both for gaming and media watching modes. Battery life is overall very efficient in travel modes/setting and no problem with media use on long haul flights. Naturally plug it in when you can.

Device feels very premium and performs incredibly well across all use cases!

reviews.title: 2 LEMONS in a row
reviews.content: The first one I purchased lasted an entire 6 days before it completely crashed and would not turn on. The replacement lasted less than 24 hours with the same issue and was so hot when it crashed that the store clerk noticed how hot it still was after it had been powered off for 45 minutes. I could have been extremely unlucky, but overall I would say this model is a total piece of TRASH. 0/10 If I could leave a negative star rating, I would.

reviews.title: Worth the purchase?
reviews.content:
Short answer yes.

People immediately point out the battery life being 6-8 hours off the charger and very dependent whether your doing office/school work or gaming. As everyone points out, gaming, you’ll get 2 hours or less depending on your settings and how many apps are running. I find it just good enough for half my school day full time until I need to plug it in when it’s on low battery. Probably could save battery with messing with the settings, but it’s alright. 

Another argued issue is the screen, some say, paying 2k and or more should have OLED. For an IPS touch screen, it’s pretty good. I have no issues playing plugged in or not plugged in. Obviously if you’re plugged in you can play at a higher graphics quality. 

I do college work on the Z13 and play titles like Total War Warhammer 3, Space Marine 2, and Arc Raiders. No issue there “when plugged in”

It’s portable, it’s powerful, and it’s just hitting every itch. 

Side Note: I have a ASUS ROG Falchion RX low profile…wayyy better for gaming when gaming instead of the actual Z13 touch pad keyboard.

reviews.title: Great purchase
reviews.content: Amazingly fast and love the form factor. Bought this to run local LLMs and it does that without sweating. Tested the latest Qwen 3.8 works like a charm.

reviews.title: Powerful, Portable, and Worth It!
reviews.content: I absolutely love the ROG Flow Z13! The performance is incredible, and it handles everything I throw at it with no problem. The 180Hz display looks amazing—everything is super smooth, sharp, and responsive. I also really like how portable it is considering how much power it has. The 64GB of memory is awesome for multitasking, gaming, and heavier programs. The touchscreen and 2-in-1 design make it even more versatile. Overall, it feels like a premium, powerful machine that I can take anywhere. Definitely one of my favorite tech purchases, and I would highly recommend it!

reviews.title: Absurdly powerful tablet
reviews.content: This thing generally blows through games and AI workloads pretty easily.  Im getting ~90 fps in Cyberpunk at native resolution (with all the FSR trickery anyway) and running some pretty large local models.  Battery life is about what you'd expect from this sort of thing.  You want a battery that lasts all day, buy a Mac.  This is not that. Windows still sucks at hibernation/sleep but I can deal with that to have something the size of a Microsoft Surface with 64GB of ram and a very serviceable graphics chipset. I actually really like the keyboard feel as well.  Keys are solid.

reviews.title: God Tier
reviews.content:
The only gaming tablet/laptop you'll ever need in my opnion.
It is so portable,so powerful (64GB of RAM!!!!)  

The fact that you can game and its equivalent to the RTX 4080.

If your getting this get the 64GB or the 128GB.

The 32GB is not worth it.
