reviews.title: Great All Round Laptop
reviews.content:
I've had this Dell 14" 2-in-1 for about three weeks now, and it's quickly become my go-to machine for both work and downtime. The 2K OLED touchscreen is the standout feature — colors are deep and accurate, blacks are truly black, and text is razor-sharp even when I'm reading for hours. Whether I'm editing photos or just browsing, the display alone makes this laptop feel premium.

Under the hood, the Intel Core Ultra 9 386H handles everything I throw at it without breaking a sweat. Multitasking across a dozen browser tabs, a video call, and a spreadsheet is completely smooth, and the integrated NPU means Copilot+ features like live captions and image generation actually run fast and locally instead of lagging. The 32GB of memory gives me plenty of headroom for heavier workloads like video editing or running a couple of virtual machines, and the 512GB SSD, while not enormous, is snappy and more than enough for my day-to-day apps and files.

Battery life has genuinely surprised me — I regularly get a full workday out of it without hunting for an outlet, which is rare for a machine this powerful.

The Celestial Blue finish is gorgeous in person: a soft, muted metallic tone that photos don't quite do justice. The chassis feels sturdy and well-built, the keyboard is comfortable for long typing sessions, and the touchscreen hinge is smooth and confidence-inspiring in tablet mode.

Overall, this is a fantastic Copilot+ PC for anyone who wants power, portability, and a stunning display in one package. Highly recommended.

reviews.title: Good everyday machine for an average user
reviews.content: Bottom line up front, this is a solid, compact laptop for everyday use. I have had no issues with its performance, I just wish it had a few changes that would make it amazing. To start off, the body of the laptop feels solid and well put together. The keyboard is a "chicklet" style with the keys separated by space. For a 14-inch laptop, the keyboard is full sized and comfortable. The keys are soft strike, meaning there is no click, and you can type on this very quietly. Not my favorite strike to be honest, but I find the keyboard fine. The surface of the laptop is one of my wished changes, it shows fingerprints and hand oils very plainly. I wouldn't ever put lotion on my hands before using this laptop. The color is s dark charcoal I think but almost skews a little blue also. The color is nice. The screen is OLED, very sharp and clear, beautiful colors, but it's very reflective also. This machine has a low blue light certification, which I appreciate, but with the reflective nature, that almost negates the benefits for me. The speakers are pretty good for such a compact package and are not visible really, I think they vent out in the hinge. The bass is limited of course as its thin form factor doesn't allow for beefy sound, and because it's on the smaller side there isn't much room on the inside. Overall though the speakers are pretty nice. I would recommend headphones or earbuds if you are consuming content (music/video). I'm super happy with the memory, coming with 32GB of memory. These days that's hard to come by for mid to low tier machines. The 3rd gen intel ultra chip in this machine screams, and also does amazing with battery life. While the graphics are integrated and aren't the most powerful, even for intel, they do a good job with very light gaming and I have no problem with performance on things like Office apps and browsers, including Chrome. I would definitely recommend this to a non-technical degree student or someone who needs a solid machine for work. I tried some CAD software and it is a little choppy with performance. I think it needs a little more graphics heft for that. As an everyday though, a solid performer.

reviews.title: Powerful Performance with Exceptional Portability!
reviews.content:
Compact laptops are indispensable. While smartphones help us with a majority of tasks, ultra-PCs particularly demonstrate this for those moments when an actual computer with a “traditional” setup is needed. Dell’s 14” 2K OLED touchscreen laptop embodies both exceptional portability and performance in a stylish package. 

As packaged:
•	Dell 14” 2K OLED Laptop
•	USB-C Power Adaptor 
•	Quick Start Guide

Weighing under 4lbs, this laptop is practically weightless and with dimensions of 12.35 x 8.82 x .61 inches, it is barely there when stowed. While portability is the central theme in my opinion, performance does not appear compromised. The Ultra 9 processor is capable of ramping up to 4.9Ghz when needed but can stay frugal to maximize battery efficiency. The PC easily handles basics tasks, streaming and video calling. My configuration has 32GB RAM installed for seamless multitasking along with 512GB solid state drive for storage. For communication, Wi-Fi 7 standard is provided should you have an access point also operating on the standard. Bluetooth is available for connecting to devices or peripherals. There are six physical ports for connectivity: 

•	3.5mm audio jack (x1)
•	HDMI 2.1 (x1)
•	USB Type A (x2)
•	USB Type C - Thunderbolt with power delivery and display port (x2)

The touchscreen OLED screen helps deliver stunning images and video. Glare is minimal and the device can be used in sunlight without issues. The OLED technology helps optimize the device’s battery performance with the 3-cell battery. For video conferencing, the 2MP IR camera provides decent performance. The speakers are downward firing located beneath the laptop. I hardly use onboard speakers but for those few instances I require their use, they are more than adequate. The touchpad is generously sized and is capable of multi-gesture. Keyboard tactile feedback is gratifying for a device this size. Two levels of brightness are available as options. 

In summary, the central theme for Dell’s 14" 2K OLED Touchscreen Laptop appears to be portability while delivering performance in my experience. The device checks all the boxes in my opinion. It appears well-built in line with the company’s reputation and should provide several years of use. I highly recommend.

reviews.title: A powerful laptop for most tasks
reviews.content:
The new Dell Ultra 9 14S laptop is a powerful device for people who need to do a bit more than the basics.  Out of the box I was impressed with how well built it feels.  Very solid, and has a little bit of heft at just over 3 pounds, with zero cheap plastic feel to it.  When initially setting up, you’re dealing with a 14 inch 2K touch OLED screen at 1920 x 1200 pixels.  Sharp and colorful but only has a peak brightness of 300 nits at 60 Hz. I would have liked to see more brightness, but indoors it looks good.  Plan on spending a fair amount of time setting the 14S up though, as initially it will download quite a few updates, and once you’re in, once you go to the update area manually in settings, there’s a huge list of more updates from major to lots of drivers and more.  All in all, I’d say I was updating for two hours (at least?), but it’s wise to do these right off the bat.

You’re getting the Intel Ultra 9 processor and 32 gids of RAM on this machine, so you do have power to do all basics plus a fair amount of video editing, and a decent amount of gaming.  Unfortunately, the graphics are of the integrated Intel type with no dedicated video card or video RAM, so you are limited a little by that, even though integrated graphics have improved a bit over time.  At this price point, I would still have liked to see some dedicated graphic RAM.  The 512 gig SSD drive gives you a decent amount of storage space. The keyboard is firm and feels good to type on.  At this size you don’t get a dedicated numeric keypad, though.  The trackpad feels good and has all of the usual shortcuts on it.  There’s no fingerprint reader key, and just a standard power button, but you can use the full res 1080p web cam to log in.  The keyboard has a backlight with (just) two brightness settings, but it gets the job done. Speakers are decent enough for your basics, and that web cam works well even in soso light but falls a little once it gets low light in the room.  More than good enough for typical online meetings, though. On one side you have a USB-A port with ear/mic jack, and on the left side you have your HDMI port, another USB-A port, and two USB-C thunderbolt 4 ports for charging and accessories.  Unfortunately, no slot for a memory card of any sort. The included 65 watt charger and cable will charge up the 14S quickly enough, and I’ve had no issues with battery life.  It will easily get you through a day and more with normal use.

The usual newer AI features come built in, like a photodirector to edit and create images, Copilot+, translation features, and more.  I haven’t had any issues with the 14S running hot or loud.  During the initial setup and downloads of new firmware and drivers, the fan kicked in a lot but hasn’t made any odd noises – just a normal fan sound that isn’t very loud.  The machine itself has (so far) never got “hot”… just a little warm when doing more demanding tasks.  It’s a comfortable laptop to use from typing to visuals, and small enough to carry around easily. Wi-Fi and Bluetooth have both been very strong with no disconnect issues at all, even from a distance from my router in my house. 

My gripes? I understand there’s a RAM And storage shortage and price war going on in the computer world, but at this price point, I repeat, would still have liked to see some dedicated video RAM and maybe a larger hard drive.  The body while very solid and nice looking, is a fingerprint magnet, but that’s a minor gripe.  I would like to see some more nits of brightness on the screen as well, but you can if you want to budget for it, get a 16 inch variant of this laptop that has a higher res screen with 400 nits, and a dedicated numeric keypad if that’s what you need.  Overall, I would still recommend the Dell 14S, though as with anything, I always say to look for it to maybe go on sale.

I also like the overall design. For a gaming laptop, it isn’t unnecessarily bulky, and the illuminated keyboard gives it the gaming look he wanted without being over the top. He’s personalized his with stickers and keycaps, so it has definitely become his computer.

Probably the best compliment I can give it as a parent is that this wasn’t one of those Christmas gifts that got a ton of attention for two weeks and then sat untouched. Months later, he’s still using it consistently and enjoying it. If you’re shopping for a teen who wants a capable gaming laptop that can also function as an everyday computer, this has been a great choice for us.

reviews.title: Solid PC, no pen included? How?!
reviews.content:
I waited a long time for this device to release, extremely excited for a Surface Pro alternative with more power, all of the features I was looking for in a creative-centered device in the most flexible form factor available. The PC overall is exactly what I was hoping for, but with one massive miss. 

All marketing for this PC included the stylus, the ASUS Pen 3.0, and stressed the quality, functionality, and experience. I was absolutely blown away to open the box after ordering on release day to find no stylus included. Something had to be wrong, as every review I'd seen had the stylus included in the box, and it's use was so aggressively advertised everywhere I'd seen reference to the PC. It's a tablet Windows PC, after all, designed for creatives. The rear cover has the pen holder integrated. There's no way that they'd sell it in other markets including the stylus, but leave it out in the US, right?

I reached out to ASUS and they confirmed that the model number includes the stylus. Connected with Best Buy per ASUS's recommendation and was told that it's not part of the package. Reach back out to ASUS, open tickets, multiple phone calls, chat sessions, emails, and finally received a response that they do NOT include the Pen 3.0 in the US release. When I expressed my frustration and asked what the solution would be, I was told that it's not available to purchase on it's own. I couldn't possibly be more blown away at how horrible of a decision this is on the part of ASUS. To then be told "we're sorry, that's frustrating, have a good day" by ASUS support has completely changed my view of the company. 

I've owned ASUS products for many, many years. This is very likely to be my last, if I end up keeping it. I wouldn't have questioned the purchase for a moment if it was $50 more and included the stylus, I can't wrap my head around the decisions made that lead to the exclusion of it in this package. Beyond that, to have absolutely zero solution in place for a customer to purchase the Pen 3.0 just shows that the priority isn't on the customer experience and overall satisfaction, and when ASUS misses the mark, they don't really care. 

If you value the ability to use a stylus that integrates well into the package (I've purchase a third party device that rattles around in the compartment as the magnetic point isn't in the right location) you'll want to look elsewhere. Of course, there are older versions of ASUS pens available, but they're expensive and fall short of the intended experience per ASUS's marketing. Spend a bit more for a very similar Surface Pro option where you have to buy your own keyboard and pen? Buy a more "standard laptop" configuration? I'm not sure of the answer as this was so very close to my perfectly ideal solution, but as of this moment I'm unable to use the device in the way that I was lead to believe I'd be able to.

reviews.title: Missing correct power supply
reviews.content:
The laptop seemed fine, the issue was the incorrect power supply was in the packaging.  This was a Open Box/Excellent deal.  I went to my local Best Buy to replace the PS and was told I needed to take the Insignia brand as a replacement.  Due to the cost of the laptop even with the discount, I wanted the specific PS that came with it.  The Manager told me I could buy the Extended Warranty for over $200 and get a new one that way.  He also suggested I could drive another 30 miles to the next store and see if they would swap out the PS on the open box they had in stock (He currently didn't have one).  However due to Best Buys new policies, you can't contact individual stores to find out if they would agree to that.

I got the impression while talking with the Manager that Best Buy is a bunch of fragmented individual stores that only help you if you purchased directly through that particular location.  So my only options being take an off brand PS, drive another 30 miles to next store, or return the item, I elected to return it.  Not the best outcome for my daughter who needs a higher end laptop for her engineering classes.  I also asked about trading it for a Brand New one and was immediately shut down, without even discussing paying up for it.  FYI the location I went to was Alamo Ranch.

reviews.title: Good Laptop!! An odd issue... tho.
reviews.content:
I don't travel, so the laptop stays plugged in all the time, so can't speak to battery life or portability.  However, the laptop is somewhat heavy, just a note there.

I started a clean slate with this laptop (and upgraded to Pro).  However, there seems to be some oddity with the mouse and typing being a bit stuttering.  Other things, too.

I got this because I'm a power user and like to have different programs open at the same time, but currently?  It's not smoooooth sailing.  Might be because the laptop and I are just getting used to each other?  Might be due to me using an usb port hub that doesn't have 2.0 usb ports for my mouse and keyboard? I've ordered a new usb port hub that does have 2 2.0 usb ports, arrives soon.  I'll find out if that's the issue or not.

But as to the laptop being SLOW to open programs - not so sure about that right now - I'm working to figure that out because I know AMD Radeon graphics are excellent and so is AMD Ryzer AI 9.  Plus 32 GB RAM.  Nothing should be slow at all.  But clearly something is happening.  Maybe defective components?  Don't know - will be testing things to figure that out.

Overall, if I ignore the slow response of opening programs - I'd say this is a good laptop to get.  I can't say it's a great laptop at this point.  If I can return to provide an update, I will do that.

reviews.title: Excellent laptop
reviews.content:
I really liked this laptop despite the fact that I returned it. I will explain the pros and the ultimate reason why I returned it. I am a niche user, the user this is intended for would LOVE it. 

Pro: 
+ 32GB RAM, it is too easy to run up against 16GB RAM limits that I dont consider anything without 32GB. My desktops have 64GB but I admit they never go past 24GB of use for what I do. 
+ Great build quality, you can lift from a corner and don't feel it flex
+ Great screen and accurate touchscreen
+ Sound/speakers are better than 98% of laptops out there
+ Great performance for this class of CPU
++ Single core performance is great, snappy system
++ Multicore performance is above average for this class of CPU
+ iGPU/graphics being the 880M from AMD is solid, not great for gaming but you can even get Fortnite going at a decent experience for a non-gaming laptop
+ USB-C charging, basically a must for me now 
+ Keyboard key travel is short in a good way. Seems a little shorter travel than the Zephyrus series but more than my Samsung Book5 pro. I prefer the shorter Samsung but this was good for I think more users. 

Cons-
- While I listed the iGPU in the Pro, it was a downgrade from my Samsung Book5 Pro 14" with the intel ARC 140V iGPU in the Intel Ultra 7 258V CPU (series 2)
- This is not used for gaming often but when I go out of town, I do use it to play Fortnite with two sons, the 880M was noticeably behind the Intel 140V. I still got the game to play well enough, highs over 100fps but every now n then there would be a stutter. 
- Fans are not loud but could be a bit better, if I chose to keep it I planned to change the thermal paste to Thermal Grizzly TG PhaseSheet PTM which did wonders on my Samsung laptop.
- Keyboard keycaps can be a little slippery. I like when keycaps have a little grip to them. Personal preference thing. 

Overall, this is an excellent chassis and a complete package for most people shopping this type of laptop. I wish Asus made it with the Intel Ultra x7 or x9 CPU series 3 CPU with Intel ARC B390, I would purchase again if they did so.

reviews.title: So far I am loving this laptop
reviews.content:
I have been using the Dell XPS 13 for about two weeks now, and overall I am really happy with it. The first thing I noticed was how light and easy it is to carry. The 13.4-inch size makes it easy to move around the house or take with me when I go out. It does not feel like I am carrying a heavy laptop.

The screen is probably my favorite feature. The 3K resolution makes everything look very sharp and clear, and the touchscreen is really responsive. I did not think I would use the touchscreen very much, but I actually use it more than I expected, especially when scrolling or browsing.

The 120Hz refresh rate makes scrolling feel very smooth too. Videos and photos look really good, and the screen is bright enough for the way I normally use it indoors.

For everyday use, the laptop has been running smoothly. I have been using it for browsing, emails, documents, video calls, streaming, and keeping several tabs open at the same time. The Intel Core 5 processor has handled all of this without any issues. The 512GB storage also gives me plenty of space for my files and apps.

The keyboard is comfortable to type on, and I like having the backlight when the room is a little dark. The speakers have also been better than I expected for a laptop this size. I have watched videos and streamed shows without needing to connect external speakers. For personal use, the sound is good and does not need to be extremely loud.

The laptop feels well made, and I like the simple design. Battery life has been good for my normal use as well. Of course, it depends on what I am doing and how much I am using the screen, but I have been happy with it so far.

The 8GB memory has been enough for what I normally do. I mostly use the laptop for everyday things, so I have not had any problems. Someone doing heavy video editing, gaming, or other demanding work may want more memory, but 8GB has been fine for me.

After using it for two weeks, the things I like most are the lightweight design, the really nice screen, the touchscreen, and the smooth performance. It is easy to carry around and comfortable to use for several hours.

So far, it has been a very convenient laptop for work, school, browsing, streaming, and other everyday tasks. I have not had any major complaints with it so far.

Now the negative. After about a week small thing a started to happen. First was the WiFi. Would randomly drop and disconnect for no reason. reviews.title: A great on the go machine for knocking out work
reviews.content:
Dell's XPS line has a well earned reputation for business productivity. Straight to the point, necessary features, reliability. This new 13.4" model is no different, but if it isn't broke, no need to fix it. 

First, let me get my gripe out of the way. There's not enough ports. This XPS model includes two USB C ports. That's it, that's all. While I partially understand as this machine is made to be light and easy tot take around (ie a ton of ports equal a ton of accessories, which is extra weight) I don't think anyone would have complained about having the option to leverage more ports. Need more accessories? You'll need an additional hub. 

With that out of the way, this laptop is phenomenal for knocking out work on the go. Per it's specs, it weights in at 2.2 pounds. Tossing it in my backpack I couldn't tell the difference between carrying it and not carrying it. Closed, it's a rather thing, sleek machine. Stylish without being extravagant. 

Open the machine up, and you have it's 13.4" 2560 x 1600 touchscreen 120 hz refresh rate screen. I'll be honest, I haven't had use for it's touch screen, but I'm not complaining about being given the option either. Would I have liked an OLED screen? Who wouldn't, but this is a beautiful LED screen which allows Dell to keep the price down. I'll take it. 

The keyboard feels crisp, which, you don't need for sign-in as the machine logins you in fairly quick with. Seeing how quickly the camera recognized and logged me in, I decided to check the camera quality out, and I was significantly impressed at the video quality considering the camera isn't something that's highlighted. With image quality like this you'll be the most detailed square in your Teams/Zoom meetings. 

The 512 GB of storage works for this laptop type. While I may have preferred 12-16 gigs of Ram, in the current state of the world, I understand. 

All in all, this 13.4" model of the Dell XPS is a great laptop for productivity on the go that I'd strongly recommend for anyone looking to pull up to their local coffee shop and knock out some home work or take a few business meetings.

reviews.title: Very nice little laptop
reviews.content:
The Dell XPS 13.4" 3K Touchscreen Laptop with Intel Core 5 Series 3 320 2026 processor, 8GB RAM and 512GB SSD Storage is a very nice little laptop to take along and use anywhere. It has a refined look that I really like. The color is what Dell calls "Sky"- to me it looks like metal-blue. It is very thin (.5") and lightweight at 2.2lbs - I can take it anywhere. I have always liked Dell's XPS line of laptops and was glad to see they have released this new laptop.

The display at 2.5K is really quite good. I streamed movies and I was impressed. This has integrated graphics, which isn't the best, but what it does have seems quite sufficient for streaming. This particular laptop also has only 8gb of RAM, which isn't usually my choice - I usually prefer at least 16gb because I tend to multi-task - stream, do email, and generally get "squirreled" and do a multitude of things without closing tabs or apps. But, the 8gb has performed well for me thus far - I am surprised. This Dell XPS laptop has a 512GB SSD drive which is sufficient for me because I tend to use clouds for storage, not the hard-drive. It has only 2 ports - both USB 3.2 Gen 2 (10 Gbps) so I can use either one for charging, using a display or whatever else I need. There isn't a headphone jack which is fine for me because I use bluetooth. But these are things to consider when buying this - if you need more than what's here, you will have issues, though there are always adapters. Dell Optimizer comes pre-loaded and needed updating, but I just don't see that it can do anything, so that's a big question mark for me. I thought it would optimize the settings for me. It also has WiFi 7 and of course, bluetooth.

The sound from the speakers that appear to be on either side, sound surprisingly good. Dell says there are quad speakers - perhaps that is why the sound is good. I love that it is touchscreen and has a backlit keyboard with chiclet keys that feel great when I type. The keys have a great feel for me and I'm not hitting extra keys like I do on some keyboards. It also has a built-in camera and is Windows-hello capable, which I rely on for security. 

Overall, the Dell XPS 13.4" 3K Touchscreen Laptop with Intel Core 5 Series 3 320 2026 processor, 8GB RAM and 512GB SSD Storage, is a quality, sturdy lightweight laptop. Nothing about it feels cheap - it is what it claims to be. I am thrilled with it, especially as an on-the-go laptop. I would absolutely recommend this to anyone in the market for a lightweight, quality everyday laptop.

q_a.question: does it come with the pen? if not what is a compatible one?
q_a.answer: No, this laptop doesn't come with a Stylus pen. It is compatible with MPP 2.0 or 2.6, like the ASUS Pen 2.0 (SA203H) and ASUS Pen (SA205H), or third-party MPP 2.0 or MPP 2.0 Stylus pen.

q_a.question: I saw the storage was upgradable. What size M.2 is it? And does it fit dual sided or single sided only NVMEs?
q_a.answer: This ProArt PX13 (HN7306EA) laptop uses a compact M.2 2230 (22mm x 30mm) form factor for its NVMe PCIe 4.0 x4 SSD slot. It fits single-sided NVMe SSDs only due to surface-mounted components positioned close to the motherboard's M.2 slot, dual-sided SSDs will not have enough physical clearance and will not fit safely.

q_a.question: Can you add storage to this later on?
q_a.answer: Yes, you can upgrade the internal storage on this ProArt PX13 (HN7306EA) laptop by replacing the existing drive, but you cannot add a second drive because there is only one M.2 slot.

q_a.question: Is there a screen protector that doesn’t affect the touchscreen sensitivity
q_a.answer: Yes, there are ultra-thin plastic film screen protectors designed specifically for the ProArt PX13 laptop from third-party seller that maintain touchscreen sensitivity without hindering touch or stylus response.

q_a.question: Can It able to work with Linux distros like Fedora KDE, Kali Linux for network and cybersecurity?
q_a.answer: Yes, the ASUS ProArt PX13 (model HN7306EA) can work with Linux distributions like Fedora KDE and Kali Linux, but you will need a very new Linux kernel (v6.12 or newer) for proper hardware support.

q_a.question: How many external monitors can this laptop support?
q_a.answer: The ASUS ProArt PX13 (model HN7306EA) laptop can support up to three external monitors simultaneously, in addition to its built-in display. The laptop has two USB 4.0 Gen 3 Type-C ports that support display output and one HDMI 2.1 port for native monitor connections.

q_a.question: What is the Wattage (100% GPU/CPU) used total? Can it be charged using USB C?
q_a.answer: This specific laptop model has a combined CPU and GPU maximum thermal design power (TDP) of roughly 115 W to 120 W. Yes, the laptop can be charged using a USB-C charger. However, there are limitations, the USB-C port supports up to 100 W of Power Delivery (PD). If you are gaming or rendering videos at 100% capacity, a 100 W USB-C charger will not be able to fully run the laptop on maximum settings. During these heavy tasks, the system may occasionally dip into the battery for extra power. USB-C charger is perfect for charging while the laptop is in sleep mode.

q_a.question: Does this come with a pen? If not, what pens are compatible and where are they in stock at Best Buy stores?
q_a.answer: It works with my Microsoft Surface pen (but did not work with the Lenovo).

I got this from open box excellent condition. Price was cut into half and this is a good deal. The Dell 16S is a premium, productivity-focused laptop with an excellent 16-inch 3K OLED touchscreen. The display is the standout: it is sharp, colorful, smooth at 120Hz, and spacious enough for multitasking, photo work, and entertainment. With an Intel Core Ultra 9 processor and 32GB of memory, it should feel very responsive for demanding office work, creative projects, and running many apps at once.

The slim aluminum design and Celestial Blue finish give it a polished, high-end feel. The biggest compromise is the 512GB SSD, which may fill quickly for anyone storing large media files or games. Overall, this is a strong choice for someone who values a large, beautiful screen, plenty of memory, and fast performance in a sleek laptop. Just plan on external or upgraded storage if 512GB is not enough for your needs.

reviews.title: Great PC
reviews.content:
My Honest Experience With the ROG Zephyrus G14

I've been using the*ROG Zephyrus G14, and my overall opinion is that it's a very good laptop—but it isn't a laptop I'd recommend to someone who doesn't want to pay attention to what their computer is doing.

The hardware is powerful, the laptop is relatively compact, and it handles demanding software extremely well. But there are definitely some things you need to understand before buying one.

The biggest thing I've learned is that **the G14 needs to be managed.

Heat Is Something You Have to Watch

The G14 can get hot. That's not something I would try to sugarcoat.

You're putting powerful CPU and GPU hardware into a relatively small laptop, so when you're actually pushing the machine, temperatures can climb quickly.

I use G-Helper to manage the different performance modes, fan behavior, and power settings. For me, this is practically essential.

I don't want my laptop running aggressively when I'm just browsing the web, writing code, or doing normal desktop work. At the same time, if I'm doing something demanding, I want the performance available.

You basically have to learn how your particular machine behaves and adjust accordingly.

 Battery Life Also Requires Attention

Battery life is another area where I wouldn't simply trust the laptop to figure everything out automatically.

If you're using conservative settings and doing normal work, battery life can be perfectly reasonable. Start pushing the CPU and GPU, though, and that battery can disappear much faster.

And this isn't limited to gaming.

One thing I've learned while using AI software is that **AI workloads can put a serious load on the GPU.

For example, I've used ComfyUI for video generation, and even though I'm not playing a game, the GPU can be working extremely hard. That means heat, fan noise, and battery consumption can all increase.

So if you're buying the G14 specifically for local AI work, don't assume that "I'm only running an AI program" means the laptop is doing something light.

 G-Helper Makes a Difference

For me, G-Helper is one of the most useful parts of the overall experience.

It gives me much more control over how the laptop behaves instead of simply letting the system run at whatever settings it decides to use.

But that's also why I'd describe the G14 as a laptop for someone who is comfortable with computers.

You need to understand what the different modes actually do. You should occasionally look at temperatures and utilization. You should understand why the fans are suddenly running hard or why the battery is draining quickly.

None of this is particularly difficult if you're technically inclined, but it can be annoying if you expect everything to be completely automatic.

 My Biggest Complaint

My biggest complaint isn't really that the G14 is incapable of something.

It's that you have to pay attention.

When I'm using it for normal work, I don't want to think about temperatures, power limits, GPU modes, or battery consumption. But with this type of hardware, especially when running AI applications, those things matter.

I've found that once I configured the laptop properly, the experience became much better.

 Would I Buy It Again?

Personally, yes—but with the same qualification.

I think the G14 is a great machine for someone who understands what they're buying

It's powerful and versatile, and I've had no problem using it for demanding applications, including local AI workloads. But I wouldn't describe it as a completely hands-off laptop.

If you're willing to learn G-Helper and keep an eye on heat, power consumption, and battery life, you can get a lot out of it.

If you want a laptop where you never have to think about any of those things, I'd look elsewhere.

My bottom line as a user: the G14 is powerful, compact, and capable, but it rewards you for knowing how to manage it. The hardware is great—you just have to remember that all that performance comes with heat and power requirements.

reviews.title: Better Alternative Than A MacBook Pro
reviews.content:
I recently purchased the 2025 ASUS ROG Zephyrus G14 with the RTX 5080 while it was on sale at Best Buy for about $2,650, versus a $3,170 MSRP.

This is my first Windows laptop. I bought it primarily as a compact mobile workstation rather than a gaming PC, although I’ll game on it occasionally. I specifically chose the 5080 for its 16GB of VRAM and additional CUDA capability. Unfortunately, it doesn’t appear ASUS will offer the same discrete 5080 in a 14-inch chassis for 2026. I hope they reconsider.

My first impression is that the $2,650 sale price is much closer to what this machine should cost. It’s excellent, but at $3,170 I would seriously consider a true mobile workstation instead.

Build quality is very good. The aluminum chassis is compact, lightweight and feels comparable to my wife’s MacBook Pro. Nothing feels cheap or like ASUS cut corners. The bottom panel is also held on with accessible screws, which should make cleaning and maintenance easier. The keyboard is responsive with a shallow, crisp feel. I’m not a fan of the light bar on the lid—it feels a little tacky to me—but that’s subjective and it can be turned off.

Performance is excellent for the size. It won’t replace my custom desktop in outright performance, but it does exactly what I expected from a 14-inch workstation-class laptop. I also haven’t experienced the stuttering, display problems or other strange behavior some owners have reported.

Armoury Crate has worked perfectly for me. In Silent mode, the G14 sips power. I’ve seen roughly 6–8 hours of light use running cloud applications such as Codex and Claude, YouTube, several Edge windows and email. The fans are often inaudible or completely off.

One important Windows 11 note: from the factory, closing the lid uses Modern Standby/Sleep, which can allow the laptop to remain active and warm. I changed the lid-close behavior to Hibernate before putting it in a bag. This is a Windows behavior, not specifically a G14 defect.

In Performance mode while unplugged, I’ve seen around 4–6 hours, probably closer to four under heavier use. The GPU understandably does not boost as aggressively on battery.

Turbo mode requires AC power and really wakes the machine up. Under sustained compute workloads I measured the RTX 5080 at essentially 99–100% utilization with power around its 120W limit. I occasionally saw brief telemetry spikes above 120W, although Armoury Crate reports a 120W maximum. More importantly, the GPU maintained its performance under sustained loads.

Thermals impressed me. With the laptop on a flat surface, the RTX 5080 generally remained in the mid-70°C range during long 99–100% GPU workloads and showed no meaningful thermal throttling. That’s impressive for this much GPU in such a small chassis. CPU-heavy workloads produced more heat, with the Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 occasionally reaching around 80°C, still well within normal operating range. Under light use I typically see the CPU around the upper 40s.

Fan behavior is also better than I expected. Silent mode is genuinely quiet. Performance and Turbo naturally get louder as workload increases, and at full load the fans are definitely loud, but the sound quality is smooth and consistent. I haven’t heard bearing noise, chatter or annoying pitch changes. They sound like a premium cooling system doing its job.

The touchpad on my unit is large, responsive and solid with none of the looseness some users have reported. The speakers are loud and crisp. The OLED display is excellent, very bright, smooth, and HDR looks fantastic.

Overall, ASUS did an impressive job fitting this level of hardware into a 14-inch machine. The compact size, 16GB RTX 5080 and strong cooling system are the biggest reasons I chose it.

At the sale price: 5/5.
At the full $3,170 MSRP: 4/5.

At the discounted price, I would absolutely recommend the G14 over the competing options I considered.
