reviews.title: 3 months of light use buyer beware
reviews.content:
I purchased this ASUS TUF Gaming F16 on June 23, 2026 for $1,782.86 at Best Buy Folsom. Within about three months — and after only roughly 10 uses total, so this is not a heavily worn machine — it developed four separate hardware faults:

Screen blackout on power switch. Every time the charger is unplugged, the display goes completely black for 3-5 seconds before coming back. This happens consistently, not occasionally, and makes the laptop unreliable to use on battery — which defeats the purpose of a laptop.
WiFi adapter randomly disappears. The wireless adapter intermittently vanishes from the system entirely — not just a dropped connection, but the adapter itself no longer being detected. The only fix is rebooting, and it recurs.
Abnormally slow boot. Boot times are far slower than any modern laptop should be, let alone a gaming machine at this price point with these specs.
Rapid battery drain. The battery drains abnormally fast even under light use, well beyond normal expectations for a machine this new.

Any one of these might be tolerable. Four of them, appearing together within three months on a $1,800 laptop used about ten times, points to a fundamentally defective unit.

On resolution: because the faults appeared after the 15-day return window, Best Buy would not refund or exchange, and directed me to ASUS. ASUS opened a support case, then confirmed in writing that their warranty is repair-only and that refunds "can only be done via your place of purchase" — pointing me straight back to Best Buy. Each company directs you to the other, and the only option offered for a nearly new, defective $1,800 machine is to mail it away for repair.

Think carefully before buying: if this unit fails outside the 15-day window and mine failed in four different ways — you will have no refund path at all.

reviews.title: A SUPER ASUS TUF Gaming A16 16" Laptop!
reviews.content:
I received the ASUS TUF Gaming A16 16"  Gaming Laptop and have been extremely happy with the speed of this laptop!  But before I get into that ....

It's always amazing to me the improvements that the Manufacturers make every year to  the packaging and setup of computer products each year.   This ASUS gaming laptop is no exception.   Packaging was sturdy and well insulated.  Everything had a "place" in the box!  The very limited "documentation" was interesting, but as it turns out, you really don't need it.

Turning on the laptop and starting the setup process was simple and easy.  It seemed like the amount of "updates" this laptop needed at setup was extremely limited, so ASUS did a great job making sure it was "current" before shipping it out to customers.

I really like the speed of this laptop.   Normally, when you have a few windows open with apps, past systems would have a tendency to "slow down" .. Not this baby!    One thing I really like - because I'm a keyboard person - is that since a 16" screen, the laptop had a separate numeric pad.   I do a lot of "number crunching" so I find all the 14" and 15" laptops  are harder for me to be efficient when using Excel.   This ASUS has a much-welcomed keyboard layout.

Even though it's a 16" laptop, it's not heavy like the older 16s" were.   I'm looking forward to using it a lot, especially since we travel frequently and I always need to have a laptop handy.

Accessing my wireless internet was a breeze and I was able to easily access my remote wireless printer with no hiccups.   The USB-C connectors were good, but I always need "one more" for things I connect to my laptop, even while traveling.

IT'S A FANTASTIC LAPTOP THAT I WOULD RECOMMEND TO ANYONE....

reviews.title: Rugged, Premium Gaming Laptop
reviews.content:
The Asus TUF A16 came packaged really nicely with a cloth sleeve around the whole laptop and another piece of cloth covering the area between the keyboard and the screen. In the box there was also the massive charger that comes with the A16 that comes in at 280W. It also came with a few user manuals including information on what speeds all of the ports are and what all of them do. It does have an ethernet port if you ever needed that. It has very good hinges compared to the older models. The laptop comes in at about 5 pounds so it's a bit heavy for a laptop. This laptop is not meant to be an everyday school or work laptop. It does have that extended area behind the hinge so it's a bit big. The setup for the TUF A16 did take a while as Windows and other updates battled it out for priority through the Windows update utility. Once I got it up and running I had to update a few more things like the Nvidia game ready drivers. This laptop comes with the Nvidia RTX 5070 which is a 50 series GPU which has all of the new DLSS technology. DLSS is an AI powered rendering technology. This technology allows you to get more FPS by having the AI fill in the gaps which also makes the game look nicer with upscaling.The RTX 5070 does only have 8gb of VRAM so it might struggle more in a few years. The laptop RTX 5070 also does not have the same performance as the desktop 5070 it is closer in performance to the RTX 4060. This laptop also comes with the AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX which is a high end laptop CPU. 
To maximize some of the premium items, the laptop comes with software called Armory Crate and that allows you to change the amount of power the laptop uses, see temperatures of the components and change if you want the laptop to use the full power of the GPU or just the integrated graphics of the CPU for better battery life. Using Armory Crate you can change the laptops performance  and after you make these changes the laptop fans will automatically adjust to the new temperatures of the laptop. A unique observation is that Armory Crate is locked in celsius and there is no way to change it to fahrenheit. You can get software other than Armory Crate if you want to change that. The A16 has great airflow with intakes being on the bottom and the exhaust on the back and you can feel the hot air being pumped out. The fans are generally not that loud but can be put on a silent mode for light work loads. I would not advise using a gaming laptop on your lap especially if you have a blanket because it ruins airflow and will cause the laptop to not be able to intake air to cool off all of the components.  The A16 does come with upgradable storage and RAM so if you buy one with 16gb of RAM you can upgrade that to 36 or 64 yourself. It comes with 2 SSD slots so you can keep the original one with windows and add another that is up to 2tb. The ASUS TUF A16 is a great mid price range gaming laptop that has a good build quality and an easy ability to upgrade RAM and Storage. This is a great feature that allows the user to upgrade to expand the longevity of this laptop, something rare among most laptop offerings.
This laptop can play most games on high to max settings with stable FPS. If it can't you can use the Nvidia DLSS technology to make the game look better and get more FPS. This laptop also excels in tasks like 3D modeling having the recommended specs for most programs. Some programs do have 32gb of Ram as the recommended specs which is where the upgradable RAM comes in clutch if you want to use software that requires 32gb of RAM.
A few random observations that I wouldn’t consider deal breakers but just something to share is the camera doesn’t have an integrated slider that covers or blocks it so it's always open.  I value privacy these days and unless you “trust” the camera to only be powered on when you want it to be you will need to add some kind of manual way to physically block the camera.  The portability is the trade off with what this laptop is designed to do, between the physical laptop size and weight but the power cable is the biggest I’ve ever had to use.  
This laptop has a very specific target market and when you really throw gaming and taxing uses like 3D printing and computer modeling software it truly is when this laptop shines.  The ability to fine tune how resources are allocated with included utility software is also helpful to ensure you are maximizing the experience and performance of the device.

reviews.title: This is a Monster Gaming Laptop!
reviews.content:
The ASUS TUF Gaming A16 16" 165Hz FHD+ Gaming Laptop with AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX 2025 processor, 16GB DDR5 Random Access Memory (RAM), NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 GPU and 512GB SSD Storage in Jaegar Gray is a monster of a gaming laptop. It is gorgeous and it is powerful! 

This laptop actually has 8gb of integrated AMD graphics AND 16gb of dedicated NVDIA GeForce RTX 5070 graphics. The two automatically switch to provide the best level of graphics that is needed for the task at hand at any given time. The GPU works with the WUXGA (FHD+) display with a high refresh rate of 165Hz. This combination works quite well for gaming which is mainly why I got this laptop. And yes, it will also be used for internet surfing, movie streaming, productivity and the like, but I wanted to make certain the specs were what I was looking for while gaming - and they are very good. A small issue I do have when I'm not using this laptop for gaming, are the WASD keys on the keyboard. It feels like they are reinforced, which is great for gamers who use the keyboard instead of a controller, but they seem a bit off when using them for typing. They seem like it takes a bit more of a press on those keys. Not a deal-breaker, but it is noticeable to me. The rest of the keyboard is really nice, even including a very small numeric keypad - at least it's a keypad, which I really like. I don't normally see a numeric keypad on a gaming laptop. The fans on this are really impressive to me. They are quiet until you really need them, and then they go on blast. But they do their job quite well - keeping the laptop cool. The fans are vented out the back of the laptop so the bottom doesn't get scorching hot like you would expect and it doesn't blow back at you. The top, bottom and right and left sides stay cool to the touch while you can feel the very warm air blow out the back. I haven't experienced this laptop getting hot at all, but as soon as I launch a game, the fans let you know they are there. They certainly do their job well! The 16gb of RAM is doing its job okay for me, though I would prefer 32gb. If I have anything else running when I start-up a game, it seems like it is pushing its limits, though I haven't had an issue with it, it just registers as a VERY large use of the RAM. The keyboard has a default setting of flashing light colors under the keys which I found to be very distracting, but after installing Armory Crate I was able to change it from the default of cycling through the colors to what I prefer, which is just a static setting in blue. There are quite a lot of settings that are able to be adjusted to your own liking from adjusting the performance to match your task, adjusting the display or the keyboard and more. As for the AMD Ryzen 9 8940 HX processor, I find it to be a very strong performer. I used to feel that Intel was the only way to go, but my mind has been changed by the new Ryzen processors. And let's talk sound - the speakers in this laptop are actually good performers with crisp and clear sound even at higher volume levels.


Overall, I think the ASUS TUF Gaming A16 16" 165Hz FHD+ Gaming Laptop with AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX 2025 processor, 16GB DDR5 Random Access Memory (RAM), NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 GPU and 512GB SSD Storage is very competitive in this space and I would definitely recommend it to anyone in the market for an exceptional gaming laptop. Plus, it comes with 2 months of Xbox Game Pass Premium to help you get started on your gaming journey.

reviews.title: ASUS - TUF Gaming A16 16" 165Hz FHD+ Gaming Laptop
reviews.content:
I was excited to try out the new ASUS - TUF Gaming A16 gaming laptop. Equipped with the latest mobile chips from AMD and Nvidia combined with ASUS' 'TUF' branding I had high expectations for how this machine would perform. 

----SETUP----

Setup was mostly straightforward. After power on, Windows 11 Out of Box Experience (OOBE) walked me through initial setups. Following that, I launched the pre-installed Armoury Crate and ensured all drives and system components were up to date. Installed Steam followed by 3DMark, Battlefield 6, Halo: Combat Evolved, and Counter-Strike 2. I used Armoury Crate to set my power profile to "turbo" to ensure maximum performance. 

----Look/Feel----

The TUF Gaming A16 has a militant aesthetic, though made of plastic, it attempts to look a bit more like steel. The keyboard itself specifically highlights  the WASD keys signaling this machine is intended for gaming. It has all of the necessary IO ports, USBC, USBA, HDMI, Ethernet, Windows Hello webcam, and a 16: 165Hz FHD display. I also went into the BIOS and turned off the hybrid GPU to ensure the Nvidia RTX 5070 would be always on. This also cuts down on the lag between switching from the integrated GPU in the AMD Ryzen chip. While these settings are great for battery life and eco modes, I wanted to focus this machine on it's gaming performance and aimed to give it the best shot at doing that possible.

----PERFORMANCE----

Initially, I ran a benchmark using 3DMark Speedway and played a round of Halo: Campaign Evolved and Battlefield 6. Performance was mediocre at best. Speedway produced a 3100 (below average), Halo on medium settings could barely keep 30 FPS on average and Battlefield 6 on "auto" (which set itself to medium-high) was unplayable. 

I thought to myself "hmm, this is weird for such high end hardware". I've been here before though, and I had an idea. I downloaded the official uninstaller for Armoury Crate and completely removed the tool. After reboot, I downloaded and installed "G-Helper" which is an alternative to Armoury Craft, without all the bloatware, necessary services and has a set of highly optimizing features for ASUS laptops. After install, I set CPU to "turbo" and GPU to "ultimate" as well as removing some remaining ASUS services. This does make the fans run at their maximum capacity due to turning everything up to their maximum capabilities while still maintaining system stability (meaning, no overclocking is done with just performance settings set to max). Re-running Speedway benchmark I achieved 3609. While not Earth shattering improvement there, Halo now ran at 110 FPS dropping closer to 70 FPS with heavier action. Battlefield 6 ran MUCH better at a constant 70 FPS on high-ultra setting, dropping to medium ran between 90 and 100 FPS. Counter-Strike 2 ran as a constant 156 FPS. Much, much better results using G-Helper. I highly recommend this to anyone wanting to maximize performance. You'll want to use a headset with noise cancellation to cut down on the fan noise, which will be pretty significant. If using the built in keyboard, you will also feel some slight vibrations. 

The 16" 165Hz display ran beautifully. It was super smooth when games could hit closer to it's maximum 165hz, such as Counter-Strike 2. Even Battlefield 6 at 70 FPS still played super smooth. Colors were very accurate and vibrant. I did not notice any screen tearing while playing. 

Aside from gaming, given such high end hardware in the A16, one could easily perform photo or video editing, graphic design, 3D modeling, AutoCAD, etc. since the hardware is fully capable. Even with the power setting scaled down a bit, these tasks perform beautifully with less fan noise. 

The touchpad and keyboard were very nice to use. Keys were very responsive and had a nice click to them. The illuminated keys shined bright with the ability to adjust intensity to preference. Touchpad was very responsive to touch and mouse movement was very smooth. 

Battery life was surprisingly good on this laptop, even with my crazy maximum setting, I was able to get about 1-2 hours on battery. That may not sound like a lot, but other laptops I've tested do not hit 1-2 hours on max setting, most are about 30 minutes. Performing more reasonable work, like video playback or streaming and the power scaled back to eco or performance, I easily got 8-12 hours. Light office work with all eco settings enabled and relying on the integrated GPU, I could squeeze out about 12 hours. This is fantastic flexibility for a gaming focused laptop. 

---CONCLUSION---

Overall, the ASUS TUF Gaming A16 is a nice latpop. Out of the box, it has crippling limitations, but can easily be overcome. The fans are extremely loud when taking full performance advantage, but it's better to be cool than overheat. It is a laptop after all. Anyone wanting extreme performance at a quieter threshold should consider a desktop instead. The A16 is aimed at on the go gaming, or those with limited space.

reviews.title: Great gaming laptop if storage isn't a concern.
reviews.content:
I've spent time with several gaming laptops over the years, and the ASUS TUF Gaming A16 strikes a great balance of performance, build quality, and price without trying to look flashy. Setup was straightforward right out of the box. After running the usual Windows 11 updates, installing the latest NVIDIA drivers, and adjusting a few settings in ASUS Armoury Crate, I was up and running quickly. The 'Jaegar Gray' finish gives it a clean, understated look that I prefer over gaming laptops covered in aggressive RGB lighting. It still looks like a gaming machine, but it wouldn't feel out of place on a desk at work or school either. The chassis also feels reassuringly sturdy, which is exactly what I'd expect from something carrying the TUF name.

Performance is easily the highlight. The Ryzen 9 8940HX is a powerhouse for a laptop in this category, and its 16 cores give the A16 plenty of overhead for gaming, multitasking, and heavier productivity work. Paired with the RTX 5070 Laptop GPU, it runs modern games extremely well at the native 1920 x 1200 resolution, and the 165Hz display is a great match for the hardware. Competitive titles feel incredibly responsive, while more demanding games still look smooth with NVIDIA features like DLSS enabled. Advanced Optimus is another feature I appreciate, since the laptop switches automatically between integrated and dedicated graphics depending on what I'm doing. You get the full performance of the RTX GPU when gaming without having to toggle modes manually every time you unplug.

I also really like the 16-inch 16:10 display itself. The extra vertical space may not sound like a big difference compared to a traditional 16:9 screen, but it's noticeable when browsing, working in documents, or juggling multiple windows. Slim bezels and a 90% screen-to-body ratio make the laptop feel more compact than you'd expect from a 16-inch machine, and everything from Windows animations to fast-paced games looks exceptionally smooth at 165Hz. The panel is Full HD+ rather than a higher-resolution QHD option, but I think that's the right call for this configuration. The RTX 5070 has a much easier time hitting high frame rates at the native resolution, and I'd rather have consistently smooth gameplay on a 165Hz screen than push unnecessary pixels and give up performance.

Cooling has impressed me as well, considering how much hardware ASUS packed inside. The combination of Arc Flow fans, multiple heat pipes, four exhaust vents, and a full-width cooling design keeps performance consistent during longer gaming sessions. As with practically every powerful gaming laptop, you'll hear the fans when the CPU and GPU are pushed hard, but the system never felt like it was struggling to stay under control. ASUS also includes anti-dust filtering, the kind of feature that's easy to overlook but should help with long-term reliability. Audio is better than I expected too. Dolby Atmos gives games and movies a noticeably wider soundstage, though I'd still reach for a good headset in competitive matches or when I want truly immersive sound.

My biggest criticism of this configuration is the storage. A 512GB SSD feels small for a gaming laptop in 2026, especially when a single AAA title can eat up well over 100GB. Between Windows, applications, and a handful of large games, the drive fills up surprisingly fast, so adding storage would probably be the first upgrade I'd consider. The 16GB of DDR5 RAM is perfectly adequate for gaming today, but anyone planning to keep this laptop for several years or use it regularly for heavier content creation may eventually want 32GB. Still, those are relatively minor compromises for the CPU and GPU you're getting.

Overall, the TUF Gaming A16 delivers where it matters most. The Ryzen 9 8940HX and RTX 5070 make a seriously capable pairing, the 165Hz 16:10 display is excellent, the cooling is well designed, and the chassis feels ready for years of regular use. For anyone who wants powerful hardware without paying extra for a fancier ROG-style design, this laptop is an easy recommendation.

reviews.title: A Powerful Laptop That Has a Few Compromises
reviews.content:
After spending time with the ASUS TUF Gaming A16, I came away pretty happy with what ASUS has managed to pack into this machine. This laptop configuration combines an AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX processor, the NVIDIA RTX 5070 Laptop GPU, 16GB of DDR5 memory, a 512GB SSD, and a 16-inch 165Hz FHD display. On paper, it is a very capable gaming laptop, and in actual use, that is exactly what it feels like. There are definitely a few compromises here, particularly with the display and storage, but after using it, I think most of those decisions make sense when you consider the hardware ASUS is prioritizing.

The first thing I noticed about the A16 is the overall design. The gray finish gives it a much more understated appearance than some other gaming laptops in the market, and I actually like that ASUS didn't cover the laptop in unnecessary RGB or aggressive “gamer” branded styling. The TUF Gaming design still gives it that gaming laptop look, but it can easily sit on a desk without looking like a spaceship. The chassis feels sturdy with almost zero flex, and at around 5 Lbs, it is certainly not the lightest, but considering the amount of hardware inside, I think the weight is reasonable for a 16in laptop. 

The keyboard is another area where I think ASUS made the right choices. The keyboard has single zone RGB backlighting rather than per key RGB, so this is not going to have that rainbow vomit lighting when you turn on your laptop, and I found it perfectly functional for gaming and everyday typing and gaming. The keys have a good amount of travel and feel responsive, and the larger chassis gives ASUS enough room for a comfortable layout with also having a number pad. The trackpad is also perfectly usable for normal Windows navigation, although anyone buying this laptop primarily for gaming is obviously going to want to use a dedicated gaming mouse. I also appreciate the selection of port options, which includes 1x HDMI 2.1, 1x Ethernet port, 3x USB-A, 2x USB-C, and a 3.5mm headset jack, making it easy to connect the laptop to a gaming monitor, wired network, peripherals, and other accessories. 

The AMD Ryzen 9 8940HX is a seriously powerful mobile CPU. It is built with AMD's Zen 4 and features 16 cores and 32 threads, with a maximum boost clock of up to 5.3GHz. This is not one of those laptop CPUs that is primarily designed to save power and the battery will get about 6 to 8 hours. Opening applications, multitasking, running multiple browser tabs, compressing files, and doing CPU heavy workloads are all things the 8940HX handles without breaking a sweat. For anyone who does more than just gaming, such as video editing, rendering, compiling, or running demanding productivity applications.

The RTX 5070 is obviously the other major reason to buy this laptop. The RTX 5070 Laptop GPU gets up to 115 watts with the turbo setting turned on with 8GB of GDDR7 VRAM. Power limits, cooling, and the individual laptop implementation can make a significant difference, and the A16's 115W configuration gives the RTX 5070 enough power to perform well. In 3DMark night raid at 1080p got a score of 70,543 which is a respectable result for a laptop in this class and in Cinebench got a score of 46,046 points which demonstrates that the GPU has plenty of performance for modern gaming.

In actual games, this is where I think the RTX 5070 makes the most sense. I was able to run modern titles comfortably using medium to high settings, and the GPU has enough power that I don't feel like I need to immediately drop everything down to low just to get playable frame rates. Games that are more demanding can benefit significantly from NVIDIA DLSS, and this is one of those laptops where I would absolutely recommend using it. With DLSS enabled, I can increase graphical settings while maintaining a much higher frame rate, and in supported games, Frame Generation also helps in that it can push the frames even more but can affect latency also, so for some competitive games, I would try not to use frame gen with those games. For competitive games such as Fortnite, CoD, Valorant, CS 2, Overwatch 2, and similar titles can take advantage of the high refresh rate, particularly when using optimized settings. For more visually demanding single-player games, I would generally run somewhere between medium and high settings and use DLSS when available. 
The display is probably my biggest nitpick for this laptop. The 16in 16:10 aspect ratio is great for laptops, and the 165Hz refresh rate is exactly what I want to see on a gaming laptop. The motion looks smooth, gaming feels responsive, but honestly I would have liked to have seen a 1440p display. The FHD+ 1920x1200 resolution isn't bad, because it makes gaming easier with the RTX 5070, but it does feel like a missed opportunity at this price point. I also would have liked to see HDR support. The lack of HDR means that even though the panel can provide a good gaming experience, it does not have the same visual punch that I have come to expect from higher end gaming laptops. 

The 16GB of RAM is another area where I have mixed feelings. For gaming today, 16GB is still usable, the system has enough raw performance to handle modern games very well. However, 32GB would have made this configuration much more appealing video editing and being more “future proof” down the road. Luckily, the TUF A16 platform has two memory slots, so upgrading the RAM later on is an option if you need more RAM. 

The 512GB SSD is probably the other specification that immediately jumps out at me. For a gaming laptop, 512GB simply isn't a lot of storage. Along with the preinstalled Bloat Ware that comes with the laptop and after you uninstall all of the apps you don't need once you start downloading  3-4 games you are basically out of storage. I definitely would have preferred at least a 1TB SSD. That said, I can understand the decision when looking at the current hardware market. Memory and SSD pricing have increased, and companies have had to make compromises somewhere to keep gaming laptops from becoming even more expensive. That being said, the A16 does have 2x M.2 SSD slots, so upgrading the storage is available.

Overall, I think the ASUS TUF Gaming A16 is a very compelling gaming laptop for someone who cares more about performance than having every premium feature. The Ryzen 9 8940HX is an absolute powerhouse, the RTX 5070 GPU performs very well, and DLSS plus Frame Generation gives the laptop even more breathing room for demanding games. The 165Hz display is smooth and perfectly usable, but I still wish ASUS had included the 1440p panel, especially considering the class of hardware inside. The lack of HDR is another disappointment, and 512GB of storage feels small for a modern gaming machine. However, both of those compromises are understandable when you consider how expensive RAM and SSDs have become and how ASUS is trying to keep the overall price under control. Overall, if you want a gaming laptop that can pretty much play everything you can't go wrong with the A16.

Pros

Excellent performance from the Ryzen 9 8940HX
RTX 5070 GPU provides strong gaming performance
165Hz refresh rate provides smooth gameplay
Good port selection
2x M.2 storage slots make future SSD upgrades easier
Upgradeable RAM

Cons

1920x1200 display 
No HDR support
512GB SSD is too small for a modern gaming laptop
Fans can get loud under heavy gaming and CPU workloads
A lot of Unneeded Bloat ware Preinstalled

reviews.title: 16GB, Small SSD, Pricey but still a contender
reviews.content:
Asus has tiers and the TUF tier is between the PRIME and STRIX line up. Well built, but don't expect too many bells and whistles.

Arriving in a basic brown box, it is stylish in print and presentation. Inside, you will get your laptop, 280w PSU, cable and a small collection of pamphlets. What you see laid out in one of my pictures is exactly what you're going to get. The TUF line provides no pack ins, cards, coins or other Asus flair that is reserved for their more premium line of laptops. You get the basics and that's it. Personally, that's not a bad thing. One thing to note is I do like the layout inside the box with a chamber to the left for the PSU and the chamber to the right for the power cord and the spartan level of literature and pack-ins nestled nicely in the center under the laptop. The well built protective cover for the laptop for shipping is nice too.

As for the A16 itself, I do like how nice the build and look of the A16 presents and it opens very smoothly. It offers an industrial metallic look that I find appealing with the TUF logo on the lid. The palm rest and keys have a super smooth, cool feel to them I like and in classic Asus style, they understood the mission and make their keyboard keys large, flat and spacious even with a numeric pad included as a plus. The only downside is the keystrokes themselves are a bit too stiff for my liking but workable. The 280w power supply is hefty but not overpoweringly so and I do like the extra long power cord. Nothing is as irritating as a short power cord which I usually have to replace almost immediately. Overall, it feels amazingly solid in the hands with low to no screen wobble nor keyboard bounce. The unit as a whole is surprisingly light in weight and easy to pick up and move around. Aesthetically and ergonomically, I am pleased.

Hardware wise, it isn't too shabby. It includes a Ryzen 9 16 core / 32 thread 8940HX processor which is basically a 7940hx which in turn is a slightly slower version of the older flagship 7945hx. It is still a more than capable CPU paired with an Nvidia RTX 5070 8GB GPU. 

The downside is going to be not only the 16GB of DDR5-5200 memory in a single stick configuration but absolutely tragic Western Digital 512GB of NVME storage. I couldn't even fit my paired down Steam directory on the A16. My 132GB World of Warcraft install (a single game) wiped out over 30% of my storage. In the end, I had to settle on World of Warcraft and my Steam directory with Fallout 76 and three other games and that left me with ~40GB free. A secondary or primary replacement SSD is almost mandatory if this is going to be a serious traveling gaming laptop. 

The 16" B16OUAN07.K IPS panel is a mixed bag. 1920x1200, 165hz and decent colors are nice, but it does not support full HDR and it is 8-bit. Still, it is more than adequate and is of entry level panel specs but I found it pleasing on the eye. Unless you're extra picky about your displays, it won't be a problem.

Performance wise it gets it done. Cinebench R23 cranked out almost 30k for multi and 1811 for single so plenty of CPU power under the hood. Timespy produced a healthy overall score of 13655 with the GPU scoring 14073 and the CPU 11690. The A16 itself uses the 115w version of the 5070. With that level of score, gaming at 1200p was excellent playing both World of Warcraft and Fallout 76 albeit to keep consistently high fps in WoW I did use level 8 vs 10 with RT enabled high.

Fans stay relatively quiet, but when pressed they can get decently loud. I've heard much louder on other gaming notebooks, but you will definitely want headphones if you're going all out.

CPU temps did peak at 93.5c which is rather toasty but the GPU topped out at 80.2.

I did find the USB-C transfer speeds to be slow when moving files from my external SanDisk Extreme 2TB NVME which can hit 1.5GB/sec on better spec'd systems. It was woefully slow on the A16.

Overall, I actually found the A16 to be a capable, well built, surprisingly compact laptop with a nice bit of punch and the 5070 pairs near perfectly with the 1200p display but the price, single stick of ram and woefully small SSD along with the slow transfer speeds knocks it down a few stars but still it is worthy enough for consideration especially if you are a fan of Asus.

reviews.title: Powerful Gaming Performance
reviews.content:
I’ve used plenty of gaming laptops over the years, but this is my first time using an ASUS TUF gaming laptop. The A16 has been very impressive so far. It balances gaming performance and everyday use really well. It has the power I expect from a gaming laptop, but it doesn’t feel like I can only use it for gaming.

The finish gives the A16 a clean look that I really like. It definitely has a gaming laptop design, but it isn’t overly flashy or covered in unnecessary lighting. I could easily use this for work without feeling like I’m carrying around something that looks like it belongs exclusively in a gaming setup. It does feel heavier than other productivity-centered laptops I’ve used, but it’s not what I would consider ‘bulky.’

The screen looked nice and sharp and honestly, it’s better than what I expected with a 1920 x 1200 (full HD+) resolution. The 165Hz refresh rate is especially nice for more premium games and even outside of gaming, I can tell the difference when scrolling through websites or moving windows around. Everything just feels smoother.

Performance is probably the biggest reason I’d consider or recommend buying the A16. The processor handled everything I threw at it without much effort. I wanted to see how it performed beyond just using it normally, so I ran several benchmarks.

In Geekbench 6, I got a 2,395 single-core score and a 14,664 multi-core score. The GPU scored 116,572 in OpenCL. I also ran Cinebench 2024, where the A16 scored 587 in single-core and 5,453 in multi-core. For AI performance, Geekbench AI gave me scores of 4,136 for Single Precision, 1,761 for Half Precision, and 8,267 for Quantized.

I ran several benchmarks to see how the A16 performs beyond just my day-to-day use. In Geekbench 6, it scored 2,395 in single-core and 14,664 in multi-core, with an OpenCL GPU score of 116,572. I also ran Cinebench 2024, where it scored 587 in single-core and 5,453 in multi-core. For AI performance, Geekbench AI returned scores of 4,136 for Single Precision, 1,761 for Half Precision, and 8,267 for Quantized.

The strong single-core scores indicate that the A16 should feel quick and responsive during everyday tasks, such as launching applications, browsing the web, and working with individual programs. The much higher multi-core scores are where the Ryzen 9 8940HX really shows its strength. With 16 cores and 32 threads, it’s well suited for demanding workloads like video editing, rendering, compiling, and heavy multitasking.

The GPU score also shows that the RTX 5070 has plenty of graphics processing power for gaming and other GPU-intensive applications. The Geekbench AI results indicate that the system also has good potential for AI-related workloads, particularly when using quantized models.

Of course, benchmarks don’t tell the entire story, but they give me a good baseline for what this hardware is capable of. More importantly, that performance translates into the real-world experience. The A16 feels extremely responsive, and I can have multiple applications running at the same time without the laptop feeling like it’s struggling to keep up.

The 512GB SSD is fast. Really fast. Using CrystalDiskMark, I measured sequential read speeds of up to 6,306 MB/s, while sequential write speeds reached 3,604 MB/s. Everything loads quickly, and I haven’t had any complaints about the drive’s performance. The capacity is another story. 512GB just doesn’t feel like a lot of storage anymore, especially on a gaming laptop. A few large games can eat up a huge chunk of that space, so I’d really like to see a 1TB SSD included in a laptop like this. Thankfully, the storage can be upgraded, so I don’t consider this a major problem. It’s just something I’d plan on doing eventually.

I’ve also been using the A16 for plenty of regular typing, not just gaming, and I’ve been comfortable with the keyboard. I tested myself on Monkeytype and managed 81 WPM with 99% accuracy. That’s obviously a personal result rather than a laptop benchmark, but it gives you an idea of how quickly I was able to get comfortable with the keyboard. The only thing I didn’t like was that I kept tapping the up arrow when I reached with my right pinky to tap the Shift key. It’s a shorter shift key so I made a lot of mistakes as I was getting used to that layout.

The speakers are very good. I ran a Dolby Atmos 5.1 surround sound test on YouTube, and I was genuinely impressed with what I heard. The volume gets plenty loud, the sound quality is very good, and the surround channels were reproduced accurately during the test. I’m not going to say the built-in speakers replace a dedicated surround sound system, but they’re good enough that I don’t feel like I have to immediately connect headphones or external speakers whenever I want to watch something.

If I do any upgrades, the two things I’ll probably look into is the storage and RAM. This model only comes with 16GB of RAM and that spec feels a little out of place. So far, it’s been fine to drive my gaming habits and productivity needs, but having a little more power under the hood would help with multitasking more. I also think the processor and GPU deserve more than 16GB of RAM.

After spending time with the ASUS TUF Gaming A16, I’ve come away pretty impressed. I’ve been able to use it for regular productivity, typing, multitasking, media, and other everyday tasks without feeling like I’m using a gaming laptop that’s being forced to do office work.

For me, the ASUS TUF Gaming A16 hits a really nice balance. I get the performance I want from a gaming laptop, but I also get a machine that’s comfortable to use for everyday work. That’s what makes this laptop stand out to me.

reviews.title: Great laptop for the money!
reviews.content:
This is a genuinely solid gaming laptop with a design that manages to feel both futuristic and classy. ASUS’s TUF series has always been known for delivering strong performance without pushing the price into premium territory, and this model continues that trend in a very balanced way. It actually reminds me a lot of my ProArt 16, because the two share several design cues - thin bezels, a slim frame, and a clean overall look that feels more professional than most gaming laptops.

The chassis is only about half an inch thick, which has pros and cons. On the positive side, it makes the laptop easy to carry around and keeps it from feeling bulky. For everyday tasks like browsing, streaming, or light productivity, the cooling system handles things well and stays fairly quiet. But once you start gaming or pushing heavier workloads, the thin design shows its limits. Temperatures climb quickly, and you can tell the cooling system is working hard. It’s not unusable by any means, but it’s something to keep in mind if you plan to game for long sessions.

Performance, however, is where this laptop really shines. The CPU is extremely powerful - 16 cores, 32 threads, and boost speeds over 5 GHz. It’s more than enough for gaming, multitasking, and even creative workloads. The RTX 5070 Laptop GPU also performs better than expected. I have the desktop version of this GPU in another system, and while the laptop variant has less VRAM, it still keeps up surprisingly well. The 8GB of VRAM might sound limiting, but for the built-in 1200p display, it’s perfectly adequate.

Speaking of the display, it’s one of the standout features. The panel looks great, colors are crisp, and the 165Hz refresh rate makes everything feel incredibly smooth - from gaming to simple scrolling. It’s a noticeable upgrade if you’re coming from a standard 60Hz or even 120Hz screen.

The only real downsides are the 16GB of RAM and 500GB SSD, which feel a bit behind modern standards. Many newer games and applications benefit from 32GB, and storage fills up quickly if you install several large titles. Fortunately, ASUS clearly anticipated this. The RAM is user-replaceable, and the laptop includes a second NVMe slot, making it easy to add more storage without replacing the original drive.

Overall, ASUS did a commendable job balancing performance, design, and price. Even with a few compromises, the laptop feels thoughtfully built and offers plenty of room to grow. If you’re looking for a capable gaming machine with a premium feel and don’t mind plugging in often or upgrading storage later, this one is absolutely worth considering.

reviews.title: Great Investment, highly recommended
reviews.content:
This is one of the best large I have made. I was one of those people who were very resistant on using any kind of AI. I came to realize that AI was going to become part of a group of skills to be had and decided I better get on board. I have to say Copilot is awesome. I am not sure about other AI platforms, I have only tinkered around with a few so far, but Copilot is a great starting point for those of us just getting started with it and seems like something that is still advanced enough for seasoned users as well.

I fell in love with the surface several years ago when i bought a used one locally through marketplace. It didn't have much memory and was well sued. I already knew going in I wanted one. 

I love the versatility of the detachable keyboard, the slim design and its features as far as operating standards go were not sacrificed for the design as is most prototypes. 

I do also love the touch screen, so helpful in many ways. I for one am not great with the touch mouse, I have become a little better at its use, however when i am having a hard time with it, the touch screen helps.

I Bought this product with a 1TB memory for use in my new business I am starting, I am hoping to find a good outer shell to purchase for it so i can use it sometimes in the field. Since I will be running a painting business there will be a lot of dust particles and things to worry about, of course this would be a concern with most computers. Again, I am excited about how easily this one travels.

Its capacity to hold on to so many things for me to work on at once is awesome, the fact that its defender program that comes with it is such a great standalone product that I haven't added a subscription to another company as of yet. This has been true of Microsoft for a long while now. I have always appreciated that.

The pen is also new to me, I haven't unlocked its full potential yet, but what I have used it for was easy and convenient.

This is a great investment, and I highly recommend it to anyone who is considering this an option.

q_a.question: Is the 16Gb ram in this laptop is 1 x 16 gb installed or 2 x 8gb installed? Please tell me Asap. And also is there an extra slot or SSD inside the laptop or not?
q_a.answer:
The RAM installed is 2×8GB modules of DDR5-5600. The brand of RAM is Samsung, and the RAM model number is M425R1GB4PB0-CWMOL.

There is only 1×M.2 2280 Gen 4 SSD slot running on x4 channels. The installed brand of SSD installed is Sandisk, which is a 512GB module with the model number SDEPNSJ-5126-1006. Some people have mentioned that their machine has a Samsung M.2 card.

If Upgrading:

Be sure to note that the RAM modules supported are 2×8GB DDR5-5600, 2×16GB DDR5-5600, and 2×32GB DDR5-4800. If you upgrade to the max capacity, you will not be able to use the Overclocked RAM speeds, and the motherboard officially supports DDR5-4800 up to 64GB total or DDR5-5600 [Overclocked] up to 32GB total.

Be sure to note that the maximum supported SSD drive capacity is 4TB, and it must be Gen 4 or earlier, this will support a Gen 5 module, but it will perform at Gen 4 speeds. Do not use a SSD with a heatsink, as it will not fit properly, and will not be cooled properly.

reviews.title: Excellent laptop
reviews.content:
I really liked this laptop despite the fact that I returned it. I will explain the pros and the ultimate reason why I returned it. I am a niche user, the user this is intended for would LOVE it. 

Pro: 
+ 32GB RAM, it is too easy to run up against 16GB RAM limits that I dont consider anything without 32GB. My desktops have 64GB but I admit they never go past 24GB of use for what I do. 
+ Great build quality, you can lift from a corner and don't feel it flex
+ Great screen and accurate touchscreen
+ Sound/speakers are better than 98% of laptops out there
+ Great performance for this class of CPU
++ Single core performance is great, snappy system
++ Multicore performance is above average for this class of CPU
+ iGPU/graphics being the 880M from AMD is solid, not great for gaming but you can even get Fortnite going at a decent experience for a non-gaming laptop
+ USB-C charging, basically a must for me now 
+ Keyboard key travel is short in a good way. Seems a little shorter travel than the Zephyrus series but more than my Samsung Book5 pro. I prefer the shorter Samsung but this was good for I think more users. 

Cons-
- While I listed the iGPU in the Pro, it was a downgrade from my Samsung Book5 Pro 14" with the intel ARC 140V iGPU in the Intel Ultra 7 258V CPU (series 2)
- This is not used for gaming often but when I go out of town, I do use it to play Fortnite with two sons, the 880M was noticeably behind the Intel 140V. I still got the game to play well enough, highs over 100fps but every now n then there would be a stutter. 
- Fans are not loud but could be a bit better, if I chose to keep it I planned to change the thermal paste to Thermal Grizzly TG PhaseSheet PTM which did wonders on my Samsung laptop.
- Keyboard keycaps can be a little slippery. I like when keycaps have a little grip to them. Personal preference thing. 

Overall, this is an excellent chassis and a complete package for most people shopping this type of laptop. I wish Asus made it with the Intel Ultra x7 or x9 CPU series 3 CPU with Intel ARC B390, I would purchase again if they did so.

q_a.question:
Does this Fire version have the text to speech feature for books? 
Does this Fire version include white text on a black background? 
Does this Fire version have a rotate screen option?
q_a.answer:
Hello jm,

Yes, the Fire HD 8 Tablet can do all of these things. First of all, in order to get Text to Speech on books in the Kindle App, I have attached the steps below:

While reading, tap the center of the screen, and then tap the menu icon Aa in the upper right corner.
Tap More, and then tap the switch next to Text-to-Speech to turn it on.

In your Kindle book, tap the screen to show the progress bar, and then tap the Play  button next to the progress bar to hear the text read aloud.
 To increase or decrease the reading speed of the Text-to-Speech voice, tap the Narration Speed  icon.
You can listen to the Text-to-Speech voice through the external speakers on your device or through your earphones plugged into the headphone jack.

In order to Display White Text on a Black Background, while in the document you are viewing, you can tap the middle of the page and the options toolbar will appear. I couldn't' be happier with this purchase, and glad I found and chose this machine at the last minute instead of paying a lot more for premium features in the Lenovo Plus 14" that I really didn't need plus a lack of ports found in that machine. reviews.title: Great laptop, fast, and excellent battery life
reviews.content:
I wanted a laptop for traveling and tried out a few others before deciding on this one. The build quality is great, it definitely feels like a premium laptop with the ceraluminum finish, the hinges feel very sturdy and don't wobble back and forth like some other laptops. Since the weight is only about 2.8lbs, it's a big plus for travel. 

The screen, like others have mentioned with these laptops, does have some glare/reflection to it, but it doesn't bother me. The screen can get very bright, which is a good thing, but I can comfortably keep it at 20-30% brightness at home and not have any issues with viewing.

Once I was able to get it setup, download all the necessary drivers, and fine-tune the text/window scaling that Windows loves to over-scale, the usability greatly increased.
The battery life is excellent. I'm used to a 15.6" Lenovo Legion Slim 7 with an RTX 3060 and max 4-5 hour of battery life (being generous of course), so when I saw 12 or 13 hours of battery remaining after a few hours of use, I was pleasantly surprised.  

Although the processor doesn't have the upgraded iGPU like the 386H and 388H, I'm still able to run Solidworks without any issues after some minor performance tweaks and allow-listing the Intel Graphics (the RAM fills up very quickly if you don't), now I barely surpass 16gb usage without any other major programs running. I can have almost a dozen Brave tabs open, Cursor IDE running, and a few other processes and still don't notice any slowdown.

The 1TB SSD was a big selling point for me rather than the 512gb being used in what seems like every laptop now. I dual-boot Linux Fedora and like to use it as a daily driver, so being able to partition off a good chunk for that, and still have plenty of room for Windows programs is very nice.

Overall, if you have the budget and don't need the upgraded iGPU like me, I would recommend at least testing this laptop out.
